content:
Seeing only outbox occurs when the app has never signed into to your accounts. The imap folder list is only downloaded after connecting to your mail provider.

You likely tapped sign-in "later" during QR code or file import, instead of tapping each acount name in turn and completing the oAuth sign-in process for each. See screen shot.

You can resolve two ways.

A)

Repeat for each account. 1. Navigate to settings > account name > fetching mail > incoming server 2. Tap next 3. Tap the Sign-in button 4. Login to your provider and grant the app permissions. 5. Navigate to settings > account name > sending mail > outgoing server 6. Tap next. Your settings will be checked.

B)

1. Reinstall the app 2. Import accounts (via QR code or file) 3. Tap each account name and complete it's sign-in flow,

content:
Hi Raphael

Q1) Why is there such a feature discrepancy between these versions?

Thunderbird for android builds upon the code base of K9-Mail, a long established open source email app, They have different development histories. There's no shared code with Thunderbird Desktop. It's comparing apples to oranges.

Over time there will likely be some feature convergence. The code base has a lot of technical debt and is a barrier currently. Modernization and refactoring of the code is underway to make future enhancements easier to apply. This is being balanced with current feature development to improve the user experience.

Q2) Why is there no warning while exporting that this will be an issue?

This is an aspect of the app being actively looked at. See link below. https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/pull/11248

Q3) Will this feature ever be added?

You can share your ideas and suggestions on Mozilla Connect where community members can vote for them.

The TB team take these into consideration when assessing the roadmap and priorities. Those voted highest have the greatest chance of being selected for development.

The below may be of interest, or you can add your own ideas. https://connect.mozilla.org/t5/ideas/thunderbird-for-android-support-per-identity-smtp-setting/idi-p/95813

1. You'll be pleased to know that archiving directly from the notification IS available. First you need to add "archive" as one of the three notification actions. Navigate to settings > general settings > notifications: Notification Actions.

Once added, an archive button will be available on the notification. See the attached screen shots.

2. I'm not a TB desktop user so not familiar with the "time stamped directory option for archiving". There's nothing in the mobile app currently beyond basic archiving.

There is a app feature under development that may be what your thinking of. It proposes to create date stamped archives, rather than time stamped ones. See the below link for more info. No guarentee if/when it will be implemented.

https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/pull/10113
